claims.text: An integrated electromagnetic-levitation, high-speed-imaging, spectroradiometry, and machine-learning platform can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change on melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The approach is applicable across a broad range of high-entropy alloys.
Containerless electromagnetic levitation in an inert atmosphere minimizes contamination.
Containerless processing minimizes nucleation on container walls.
Containerless melting establishes a clean, homogeneous liquid-phase interface.
Optical and radiative signals directly reflect melting onset, latent heat, and volume change.
High-speed multisignal acquisition captures the rapid kinetics of melting.
Machine-learning surrogate models trained on ab initio molecular dynamics and calibrated on binary and ternary systems can interpret the measured thermal signatures of complex HEAs.
Such machine-learning models can interpolate or extrapolate thermal signatures to extract fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting-point shifts in HEAs.
The method can determine melting temperature and fusion thermodynamics with errors below ±5% relative to conventional DSC benchmarks.
The method provides reliable measurements of volume change on melting.
The proposed approach is more efficient and precise than traditional contact-based calorimetry.
Traditional contact-based calorimetry typically has approximately 10–15% uncertainty.
Container-based DSC is slower and is subject to contamination and nucleation artifacts.
The proposed method is applicable to single-phase HEAs with melting temperatures up to approximately 2500 K.
The proposed method is applicable only when oxide and impurity levels are limited or modest.
Performance may degrade for alloys with multiple overlapping phase transformations or compositions outside the machine-learning calibration domain.
Microsecond-scale acquisition is sufficient to resolve rapid melting transitions.
Volume change can be obtained from high-speed image analysis correlated with density changes.

contradictions.description: DSC is characterized as having approximately 10–15% uncertainty, yet agreement with DSC within ±5% is used both as the performance target and as a decisive rejection threshold. A benchmark with the stated uncertainty cannot by itself adjudicate a ±5% error threshold.

The proposed levitation platform specifies optical imaging and radiometry but no calorimetric detector or explicit energy-balance method, whereas the validation plan says fusion enthalpy and entropy will be obtained by integrating a calorimetric signal. The source of that signal is therefore internally unclear.
